name: Trend Following
rationale: Trend-following rules try to participate in persistent uptrends and reduce exposure during sustained declines.
expected_benefit: Lower drawdown and calmer equity curves than buy-and-hold, with the explicit trade-off that total return may lag during strong bull markets.
failure_modes: Underperformance when the benchmark spends long periods above the trend filter.
False comfort if adjusted-price and benchmark economics are inconsistent.

canonical_variants.name: Single-asset SMA long/cash
canonical_variants.description: Hold the asset when close is above a long simple moving average and move to cash when close is below it.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A daily 200-day SMA trend strategy may reduce maximum drawdown versus buy-and-hold while retaining most long-term growth.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Retain at least 80% of benchmark CAGR while reducing max drawdown by at least 25% relative after realistic costs.

canonical_variants.name: Rolling breakout long/cash
canonical_variants.description: Enter after price breaks above a rolling high and exit after it breaks below a rolling low or trend filter.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A daily breakout trend strategy may capture persistent upside moves while avoiding some large declines.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve risk-adjusted return without materially increasing max drawdown after realistic costs.

suggested_validation: Run cost sensitivity with realistic liquid ETF assumptions.
Run date-window sensitivity across preselected market regimes.
Run train/test or walk-forward validation before accepting any tuned parameter.
references: Hurst, Ooi, and Pedersen, A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing
Moskowitz, Ooi, and Pedersen, Time Series Momentum
execution_notes: The engine can execute daily long/cash SMA, EMA, and rolling breakout variants. It does not currently support shorting or intraday stop execution.
